correctness.rationale: The proof derives the exact base-polytope description by convex mixtures of bases from pairs of parallel classes. For at least three classes, each nonnegative coordinate has vertex maximum one and each class sum has vertex minimum zero, yielding exact necessary-and-sufficient reflection constraints. Feasibility of class-sum intervals gives the maximum of three obstructions; the two-class case is exactly a product of simplices. Direct relative-interior arguments prove all affine-dimension branches. The standard-library exact-rational verifier checked 2036 profiles / 77808 reflected vertices; an independent general-rank-inequality LP matched 247 profiles. Computations are finite corroboration, not the universal proof.

value.rationale: A natural affine-geometric invariant is evaluated over the complete class of finite rank-two matroid base polytopes, characterized by parallel-class sizes. The result resolves all optimal-center sets and their affine dimensions, exposes three sharp competing obstructions, and distinguishes connected nonunique-center examples from uniformly dense/hypersimplex cases. This exact classification is not a known Ehrhart table, a trivial renaming, or a numerical example; it supplies an explicit, interpretable benchmark for general polyhedral-center optimization.
